title: Preparation of fluorescent in situ hybridisation probes without the need for optimisation of fragmentation
author: McCoy, Costello, et al.
materials: To obtain microgram amounts of BAC DNA of suitable quality for FISH probe generation we modified the protocol of QIAGEN plasmid mini kit (QIAGEN, Melbourne, Australia) (see supplemental material). This method routinely yields more than 10ug of pure BAC DNA from 50 ml of starter culture. Columns used for preparation are able to be recycled as described in Siddappa et al. [4]. In summary, this method uses an alkaline lysis method where QIAGEN neutralisation buffer P3 is replaced with buffer N3 and BAC DNA is precipitated from the lysate with isopropanol before being resuspended in buffer QBT then loaded onto the P20 microtip. Samples precipitated with buffer N3 perform better than buffer P3 in that they are easier to resuspend and contain less material that impedes flow of the material through the column. Following column washing and elution, DNA can be spooled out of the elution buffer by addition of isopropanol.

In order to determine the restriction enzymes suitable for fragmentation of BAC DNA to an appropriate size we selected a series of enzymes with 4bp recognition sites and the same optimal digestion buffer and tested them individually and in combination on two different BAC constructs as well as human and mouse genomic DNA (Table 1) (New England Biolabs enzymes from Genesearch, Arundel, Australia). Restriction enzymes with a 4bp recognition sequence will theoretically cut a random sequence of DNA every 44 = 256bp. In practise, we found this not to be the case and to achieve fragmentation to the desired 500bp-200bp it was necessary to use a combination of two enzymes (Fig. 1). From our initial test we identified 5 enzyme combinations that exhibited promise for fragmenting DNA to the desired range of 200-500bp. These were then assessed in a side by side comparison of 6 human BAC constructs (CHORI RP11 human sequence insert BACs were sourced from MCRI, Melbourne, Australia) and human and mouse genomic DNA (Fig. 1). Detailed methods for probe preparation are provided in the supplementary material. In brief, 1.5ug of each fragmented BAC was labelled with platinated fluorescent dyes using the universal linkage system from KREATECH (Diagnostic Technology, Belrose, Australia). RP11-825A8 was labelled 550 red/orange and RP11-35C4 was labelled with 495 green. Unincorporated fluorophore was removed using KREApure columns provided with the labelling reagent. DNA concentration and dye absorbance of the labelled material was quantitated on a Nanodrop (Thermofisher Scientific, Scoresby, Australia) and this was used to determine the degree of labelling. 1 μg of 495 green and 300 ng of 550 red/orange probes were combined with 25 ng Cot-1 DNA (Thermofisher Scientific, Scoresby, Australia) (to block non-specific binding) and this was ethanol precipitated then resuspended in 48 μl LSI/WCP hybridisation buffer (Abbott, Lane Cove, Australia). 2 μl of this was used in each hybridisation reaction. Total price of probes per FISH including DNA preparation, digest, clean up, labelling and resuspension is approximately $8.36 compared with $102.85 for commercial equivalent probes.

steps.title: Isolate BAC DNA
steps.instruction: Obtain microgram‑scale BAC DNA using a modified QIAGEN plasmid mini‑kit protocol.

substeps.instruction: Streak glycerol stock onto LB agar containing 10 µg/ml chloramphenicol; incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Pick a single colony and grow in 2 ml LB + antibiotic at 37 °C for a full day.
Inoculate 1 ml of this overnight culture into 50 ml LB + antibiotic; grow overnight at 37 °C.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 6,000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the pellet thoroughly in 5 ml resuspension buffer.
Add 5 ml lysis buffer, invert the tube gently 7 times, and place on ice for 10 min.
Add 7 ml Guanidine‑HCl neutralisation buffer (buffer N3), invert gently 7 times, and keep on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C (swinging‑bucket rotor); transfer the clear supernatant to a clean tube and repeat the spin.
Add 13 ml isopropanol to the pooled supernatant, invert gently 7 times, and place on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C; discard the supernatant.
Wash the DNA pellet with 750 µl 70 % ethanol, gently invert to release the pellet, transfer to a 1.5 ml tube; repeat with a second 750 µl 70 % ethanol wash.
Spin at 6,000 rpm for 5 min in a micro‑centrifuge; discard ethanol.
Air‑dry the pellet for 10 min (do not over‑dry).
Resuspend the pellet in 500 µl molecular‑grade water; flick gently, do not vortex.
Add the resuspended DNA to 500 µl QBT buffer (QIAGEN plasmid mini‑kit).
Purify on QIAGEN P20 columns (columns may be recycled as described by Siddappa et al.) using the QBT suspension in place of clarified lysate; follow the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute DNA in 800 µl EB buffer into a 1.5 ml tube.
Add 650 µl isopropanol, invert gently until DNA spools out of solution.
Briefly spin, discard supernatant, add 500 µl 70 % ethanol, invert gently.
Spin briefly, discard supernatant, air‑dry until just dry (avoid over‑drying).
Resuspend the purified BAC DNA in 50 µl molecular‑grade water. Expected yield >5 µg.

steps.title: Digest BAC DNA
steps.instruction: Fragment the purified BAC DNA to 200‑500 bp using a CviQI/AluI restriction‑enzyme cocktail.

substeps.instruction: In a reaction tube combine 500 ng BAC DNA, NEB Buffer 4 supplemented with BSA, and 5 U of CviQI plus 5 U of AluI (total volume as recommended by the enzyme supplier, e.g., 20 µl).
Incubate 1 h at 25 °C (CviQI activity).
Immediately follow with 1 h incubation at 37 °C (AluI activity) to complete digestion.
Optional: verify fragment size (200‑500 bp) on a 1 % agarose gel.

steps.title: Label DNA with fluorescent dyes
steps.instruction: Label the fragmented BAC DNA using the KREATECH Universal Linkage System and remove excess dye.

substeps.instruction: Take 1.5 µg of each digested BAC fragment.
Label RP11‑825A8 with the 550 nm red/orange platinated dye and RP11‑35C4 with the 495 nm green platinated dye according to the KREATECH kit protocol.
Purify each labeled product with the supplied KREApure column to remove unincorporated fluorophore.
Measure DNA concentration and dye absorbance on a Nanodrop (ThermoFisher Scientific, Scoresby, Australia) to determine degree of labeling.

steps.title: Prepare mixed probe mixture
steps.instruction: Combine labeled probes with Cot‑1 DNA, precipitate, and resuspend in hybridisation buffer.

substeps.instruction: In a micro‑centrifuge tube add 1 µg green‑labeled probe, 300 ng red/orange‑labeled probe, and 25 ng Cot‑1 DNA.
Add 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate, pH 4.6, then add three volumes of 100 % ethanol; mix gently.
Incubate at –20 °C for >1 h to precipitate nucleic acids.
Centrifuge at 13,200 rpm for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 500 µl 70 % ethanol, invert gently, then centrifuge at 13,200 rpm for 5 min.
Air‑dry the pellet briefly, then resuspend in 48 µl LSI/WCP hybridisation buffer (Abbott Vysis).
Store at –20 °C or use immediately; 2 µl of this mixture is used per hybridisation slide.

steps.title: Hybridise probes to slides
steps.instruction: Prepare cell slides, denature, and hybridise the probe mixture overnight.

substeps.instruction: Harvest cells, perform hypotonic lysis, fix in acetic acid/methanol, and drop onto microscope slides.
Air‑dry slides, age in 2 × SSC for 2 min, then dehydrate through an ethanol series (70 %, 85 %, 100 %, 2 min each) and air‑dry.
Apply 2 µl of the probe mixture (from previous step) to the hybridisation area.
Cover with a 13 mm round coverslip and seal with rubber cement.
Denature by heating at 80 °C for 15 min.
Incubate slides overnight at 37 °C in a humidified chamber.

steps.title: Post‑hybridisation wash and mount
steps.instruction: Wash slides, air‑dry, and mount with antifade medium for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Wash slides in 0.4 × SSC/0.3 % NP‑40 at 73 °C for 2 min.
Wash in 2 × SSC/0.1 % (NP‑40) at room temperature for 1 min.
Air‑dry slides in the dark.
Mount with DAPI II antifade mounting medium (Abbott, Lane Cove, Australia) containing DAPI counterstain.
Visualise fluorescence on a microscope; capture images and process with ImageJ.

description: Production of FISH probes from large genomic insert vectors requires extensive optimisation to produce 200-500bp fragments. Here we demonstrate that suitable fragmentation can be achieved using a cocktail of the restriction enzymes CviQI and AluI.
